description: The Canadian Wetland Inventory is a national framework, established in 2002 by Ducks Unlimited Canada, Environment Canada, the Canadian Space Agency and the North American Wetlands Conservation Council, for mapping Canada's wetlands consistently, since the country has no complete wetland inventory. The page read on 2026-09-28 explains that DUC has inventoried wetlands from aerial photography and satellite imagery since 1979, has completed inventories in the Boreal and Prairie ecozones and the St. Lawrence Lowlands, and uses a data model based on the Canadian Wetland Classification System (shallow water, marsh, swamp, fen and bog), downloadable as a PDF; a CWI Progress Map shows completed and ongoing inventory areas and, where released, detailed wetland polygons with source and partner information. Coverage is partial national. Access is free through the map; no licence is stated and download options depend on each partner dataset. Caveats: coverage is incomplete and methods differ by project year. It supports nature-based flood protection and exposure studies, such as wetland storage upstream of roads and settlements. Related records: data-duc-boreal-enhanced-wetland-classification is the boreal part of the inventory.
